payload.build_machine:
Seeded machines/it/machine-build-steps.canvas: start -> c1_classifier -> c2_milestone_lane -> c3_atomic_close -> c4_bless_wiring -> c5_provisioning -> done. Five chunks, each with realization: engine-ts and a what_landed + run_ref evidence form.

DEPENDENCY EDGES, and where they are real rather than merely drawn: c3 genuinely depends on c1, because the close cannot filter without the classifier. c4 genuinely depends on c2, because the bless path calls the milestone lane. c5 is INDEPENDENT of c1-c4 - it touches provisioning only - and c1 and c2 are independent of each other. The drawing serialises them because one agent is building; the honest statement is that {c1, c2, c5} could run in parallel and {c3, c4} follow their prerequisites. Recording that rather than pretending a chain, since parallelism is exactly what this line of work is meant to unlock.

Chunk sizing is deliberately small and resumable: c1 is a pure function with no git; c2 is one git-driving helper; c3 is the ordered close; c4 is a wiring change on the bless path; c5 is provisioning. An interruption loses at most one chunk.
payload.promotions_placed: Both promotions are placed rather than left as notes. P1 - THE ROOT-RESOLUTION RULE (drive git with an explicit worktree target, never the caller's cwd) enters AS c2's implementation, named in its guidance, because that is the chunk where getting it wrong would reproduce yesterday's trunk-versus-worktree defect on the bless path. P2 - SP2's FIXTURE SHAPE (a provisioned worktree, several milestones each carrying claims and events, then a close) has already entered as the acceptance scenario inside the authored checks, so c3 begins against a pre-verified scaffold rather than an invented one. The six fitness candidates map onto the chunks: FC1 and FC2 to c3, FC3 to c3's reachability assertions, FC4 and FC5 to c3's two refusal paths, FC6 to c2.
